title: Silver Anchor QA onramp scratch
content:
Context:
- Silver Anchor: small-mid fintech (account aggregation + KYC assist). Interested in Private deployment (VPC) with optional on-prem later. Must meet strict dataplane separation (per-tenant isolation) and tie into their HSM for PII keying. Pilot scope = POC for KYC flows + human-in-the-loop review augmentation.

Last call (2024-11-07) participants:
- Silver Anchor: Tom Becker (CTO), Asha Kulkarni (Lead Eng), Ben Ito (Security), Clara Ruiz (Product)
- Redwood: Maya Patel (CS), Diego Ramirez (Solutions Eng), Liu Chen (SRE consultant)

High-level asks / acceptance criteria (captured live):
1) Data residency & security:
   - All request/response payloads for pilot must live in Silver Anchor VPC; no tokenized PII can leave network unless explicit (opt-in).
   - HSM integration for encryption of stored artifacts and signing of request IDs.
2) Latency SLOs:
   - 95th percentile (p95) under 220ms for single utterance generation (short prompts, ~80 tokens) in regular load.
   - Burst tolerance: occasional spikes up to 4k qps for 30s with graceful fallback (degraded models or async queue).
3) Quality / model controls:
   - Need model pinning per route and deterministic rollout (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%).
   - Prompt templating + a simple eval harness: 12 test prompts covering red-teaming and edge cases.
4) Observability:
   - Request-level logs (redacted PII), token-level cost estimates; traceability to model version and kernel/quant profile used.

Initial technical sketch (notes):
- Deployment: Redwood Private in Silver Anchor VPC. Control plane lives in Redwood managed account but control plane endpoints must support mTLS and allow Silver Anchor IP ranges for webhooks.
- HSM: they use AWS CloudHSM (customer-managed). We need to verify our KMS/HSM integration path: options
   A) Redwood uses customer's AWS KMS CMK to wrap model cache keys and stored artefacts (preferred)
   B) If not possible for pilot, use envelope encryption where Redwood holds ephemeral key but Silver Anchor rotates master key monthly.
- Networking: Strict egress rules. Need a pre-flight network runbook for firewall rules + NAT gateways. Confirm whether private endpoints for metrics ingestion are acceptable (they asked for no public metrics egress).
- Auth: mutual TLS for the control plane and token-based local agent for dataplane calls. Discussed short-lived local tokens (~15m) issued by control plane with HSM-backed signing.

Performance considerations & gotchas (observed from other pilots):
- KV cache warm-up: first-day latency spike if we don't pre-warm frequent prefixes. Suggest a small warm-up job seeded with last-30-day top queries (we should get sample).
- Large-batch optimization conflicts with strict p95 latency. For low-latency routes, set batch window 5–10ms and cap batch size; use separate GPU pool for high-throughput reranking jobs.
- Quantization regression: 4-bit quantization gave ~2–3% quality regressions on a comparator set during earlier test — ensure we have model/quant profiles per-route and a rollback plan.
- Tokenization mismatch: client pipelines using custom tokenizers caused off-by-one truncation; ask Silver Anchor to confirm tokenizer version and provide sample messages.

Minimal pilot architecture (practical):
1) Dedicated Redwood Private instance inside Silver Anchor VPC (single AZ to start)
2) Small GPU pool (1-2 GPUs, 8–16 core equivalent) for synchronous inference + separate small pool for async job queue
3) HSM/KMS integration for data-at-rest
4) Canary routing config: control plane routes 5% traffic to canary variant with slow-failover policies
5) Observability: Redaction pipeline + metrics to Silver Anchor internal Grafana via VPC peering (or push to private metrics endpoint)

Operational plan & timeline (draft):
- Week 0: Preflight network check, access provisioning, confirm HSM keys + IAM roles (owner: Ben Ito)
- Week 1: Deploy private control plane connectors + small GPU pool; basic smoke tests (owner: Diego)
- Week 2: Run warm-up job, integrate token signing, execute 12-test prompt evals (owner: Liu)
- Week 3: Canary enabled (5%), monitor quality/latency 72h -> expand to 25% if no regressions (owner: Maya)
- Week 4: Post-canal review and prepare SLO docs, handover to Silver Anchor ops (owner: Asha)

Open questions for Silver Anchor (need answers before week 0):
- Confirm whether CloudHSM CMK policy allows Redwood to call Encrypt/Decrypt with a service principal (Ben to confirm).
- Provide representative sample of top-500 queries (anonymized) for cache warm-up and batching tuning.
- Confirm telemetry egress policy: can we push metrics over a private endpoint or must we expose a pull endpoint inside their network?
- Do they want token-level cost logs exported to their billing pipeline or is a summarized daily report enough for pilot?

Action items (short):
- Maya: draft pilot SOW with explicit HSM integration options and ship to Tom by 2024-11-12.
- Diego: create warm-up job template and share terraform snippet for firewall rules (due 2024-11-13).
- Liu: prepare small smoke test harness + 12-eval prompts repo; include an example of token redaction (due 2024-11-14).
- Ben (Silver Anchor): confirm HSM policy and share sample anonymized query set (target 2024-11-13).

Notes-to-self / heuristics for onsite engineers:
- If they insist on per-tenant physical isolation, be ready to propose multi-tenant with strict namespaces first (faster), then convert to full dedicated stacks in next phase.
- For early QA, use the hosted smaller model variant for background/bulk tasks, but require strict routing rules so protected routes never hit hosted endpoints.
- Document the exact tokenizer and byte-pair vocabulary used; save a test harness that asserts token counts match client expectations.

Slack / threads references:
- slack: #customer-silver-anchor (ask Tom to invite Diego + Maya)
- internal thread: thread/RED-2876-HSM-discuss

Bottom line (one-liner to share with account exec):
Silver Anchor pilot is technically feasible with Redwood Private, requires HSM/KMS policy confirmation and a short warm-up + canary cadence to meet p95 latency goals; focus next week on HSM policy + sample queries to tune caching.
